title: MA2H GET Message Body (v0.5)
description: Body of GET /v1/messages/{id}: the original message plus current `status`, the Hub-assigned `id`, and (once terminal) the embedded `response`.

allOf.$comment: An ask/task's top-level status is ALWAYS the §7 resolution track (spec §8.2/§14.2) — mailbox states (queued/bounced/acknowledged/delivered) live under `mailbox`; a bounce surfaces here only as its cancelled/dismissed auto-resolution.
A human-inbox notify is delivered-on-acceptance (spec §5.1) and has no other state.
An addressed notify's lifecycle IS the §14.2 delivery track (spec §5.1).
The mailbox track exists only for ADDRESSED messages (spec §14.2); a human-inbox message has no outbound mailbox leg.

Every ADDRESSED message carries its authoritative outbound track (spec §8.2): the inter-agent leg requires the §14 primitive, so the track always exists — a sender must never be left unable to distinguish queued/delivered/bounced/expired.

The msg_ ack-key namespace (spec §8.7.1) is normative for v0.5-minted message ids — mirrors the res_ conditional in response.schema.json; pre-0.5 messages keep their opaque ids (unchanged-wire contract).

The response-track terminal `expired` is a v0.5 state (spec §14.2): a 0.3/0.4 message keeps its unchanged wire, on which the track never expires — the validator must not approve a legacy body carrying a state its own minor does not define.

An undeliverable mailbox terminal on an addressed ask/task guarantees a resolution terminal (spec §7/§14.2): the system:undeliverable auto-resolution fires, or a pre-death resolution already won the CAS (bounced + answered is legitimate — resolved, never acked, then died). What can never be true is `open`: a permanently undeliverable request must not present as actionable.

The response track exists only after resolution (answered -> delivered-to-agent -> ..., spec §14.2): a body claiming response-delivery states for a still-open request would assert delivery of a nonexistent answer.
A notify has no response track — nothing routes back (spec §5.1); an addressed notify's consumption lives on `mailbox`.

id.description: Hub-assigned canonical message id. v0.5-minted ids are in the msg_ ack-key namespace (the conditional below, spec §8.7.1); pre-0.5 ids are grandfathered.

status.description: Lifecycle status (spec §7). v0.5 adds `queued`/`bounced`/`acknowledged` for ADDRESSED messages: an addressed notify's lifecycle IS the delivery track (queued -> delivered -> acknowledged, or terminal bounced/expired, spec §14.2); an addressed ask/task keeps the §7 resolution machinery here (open -> terminals — an undeliverable track terminal auto-resolves it cancelled/dismissed) with the outbound track surfaced under `mailbox` and the response track under `delivery`.

response.description: Present once the message is terminal (ask/task). Embeds the full Response envelope.

delivery.description: The RESPONSE track (spec §14.2), for ask/task of either leg: did the submitting party get the answer (delivered-to-agent -> acknowledged, plus the v0.5 terminal `expired` = the answer was NEVER seen). Orthogonal to `status`/`response`; present on a Hub offering the ack primitive. For an ADDRESSED ask/task this coexists with the v0.5 `mailbox` object (the outbound track); a notify has no response track (see `mailbox`).

delivered_at.description: When the receiving party got the message (mailbox entry drained, or Response push-2xx / agent GET).

ack.description: The ack envelope, present once state is `acknowledged`.

allOf.$comment: Delivery honesty (spec §14.2): a track `expired` MUST mean NEVER delivered — a body claiming both would be the exact false belief the track exists to kill.

mailbox.description: v0.5: the outbound MAILBOX track of an ADDRESSED message on the sender's authoritative §8.2 pull (queued -> delivered -> acknowledged, or terminal bounced/expired, spec §14.2) — did the ADDRESSEE see it. Present only when `to` is present (the root conditional). On `bounced`, a present `delivered_at` means seen-then-orphaned and an absent one never-seen (the receipt `prior` distinction, spec §8.7.1). For an addressed notify this track IS the lifecycle (`status` mirrors it, spec §5.1); for an addressed ask/task it coexists with the response-track `delivery` object.

delivered_at.description: When the addressee's drain first delivered the entry (spec §14.2; a stream push alone does not stamp it, spec §8.7.2).

allOf.$comment: Mailbox honesty (spec §14.2): queued = not delivered yet; a track `expired` MUST mean NEVER delivered. bounced deliberately allows delivered_at: presence = seen-then-orphaned, absence = never-seen.
